description: Honours and records of 21 footballers, parsed from English Wikipedia 'Honours' sections (raw wikitext) and cross-checked against Wikipedia list articles and RSSSF. Only titles/awards listed as won are counted; runner-up/third-place finishes, youth, state, lower-tier, managerial and retrospective/honorary items are listed separately and not counted.

definitions.league_titles: Top-flight national league championships. MLS Cup and NASL Soccer Bowl count as the US league title; the MLS Supporters' Shield, Brazilian state championships (Paulista, Carioca, Mineiro, Gaúcho), the colonial Mozambique provincial championship and lower divisions are not counted.
definitions.distinct_countries_league_title: Number of different countries in league_titles.by_country.
definitions.distinct_leagues_top_scorer: Number of different top-flight leagues in which the player was the league's top scorer (Pichichi, Premier League Golden Boot, Capocannoniere, Torjägerkanone, etc.); state championships, cups and second tiers excluded.
definitions.ballon_dor: France Football Ballon d'Or incl. the 2010–15 FIFA Ballon d'Or; podiums from the Ballon d'Or article winners table.
definitions.ucl: European Cup/UEFA Champions League proper (qualifying rounds excluded); titles from the player's honours list.

caveats: Everything reflects English Wikipedia as fetched on the dates in fetched_at (2026-10-30). Recent items (2025–26 season titles, 2026 FIFA World Cup awards, 2026 Ballon d'Or) were cross-checked only against other Wikipedia articles fetched the same day (see each player's notes) and a small number of web searches recorded in the agent report; re-verify before publication.
Counts include every competition in each category without judging which trophies are 'major'; minor, regional, unofficial, youth and state-level items are listed under team_honours.not_counted.

ucl.source: Wikipedia Pelé infobox: clubs Santos (1956–1974) and New York Cosmos (1975–1977) only; never played for a European club, so no European Cup/UCL matches.

notes: Pelé's six 'Campeonato Brasileiro Série A' titles are the 1961–65 Taça Brasil and the 1968 Torneio Roberto Gomes Pedrosa, retroactively unified with the national championship by the CBF (2010); likewise his 1961, 1963 and 1964 'Série A top scorer' awards are Taça Brasil top-scorer awards. Excluding the unified titles, his only national-league title is the 1977 NASL (Soccer Bowl) with New York Cosmos and he has no national-league top-scorer award.

His 10 Campeonato Paulista titles and 11 Paulista top-scorer awards are state-level and not counted as top-flight league honours here; the 'France Football Ballon d'Or' years listed on his page are the retrospective 'Le nouveau palmarès', not awards (he was ineligible: non-European).
Not counted as top-flight league titles: Campeonato Paulista (São Paulo state) ×10 (1958, 1960, 1961, 1962, 1964, 1965, 1967, 1968, 1969, 1973).
World Cup 'Golden Ball' [1970] listed on the player page predates the official award (1982); treated as retrospective.
